questions.question_text: Which of the following disease is treated with Penicillamine ?
questions.explanation: Penicillamine is a chelating agent used to remove excess copper in Wilson's disease.

questions.question_text: Aluminium hydroxide gel is assayed by
questions.explanation: Aluminium hydroxide is typically assayed using complexometric titration with EDTA.

questions.question_text: An important ingredient used in commercial sun-tan preparation is
questions.explanation: Zinc oxide and titanium dioxide are widely used physical UV blockers in sunscreens.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drug is used in cough mixtures ?
questions.explanation: Potassium iodide is used as an expectorant in cough mixtures.

questions.question_text: Gutzeit test is used for the limit test for
questions.explanation: The Gutzeit test is a specific chemical test used for the limit test of arsenic.

questions.question_text: Alkaline potassium mercuric iodide is known as
questions.explanation: Nessler's reagent is an alkaline solution of potassium mercuric iodide used to detect ammonia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used in antidandruff preparations ?
questions.explanation: Selenium sulphide is a common active ingredient in antidandruff shampoos.

questions.question_text: The reddish purple colour formed in limit test for iron is
questions.explanation: In the limit test for iron, iron reacts with thioglycollic acid in the presence of citric acid to form a reddish-purple ferric thioglycollate complex.

questions.question_text: What is Epsom salt ?
questions.explanation: Epsom salt is chemically known as magnesium sulphate heptahydrate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drug is used as antidote in arsenic poisoning ?
questions.explanation: Dimercaprol (BAL) is a classic chelating agent used as an antidote for arsenic, mercury, and lead poisoning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a tropane alkaloid ?
questions.explanation: Hyoscyamine possesses a tropane ring structure and belongs to the tropane alkaloid class.

questions.question_text: Which of the opium alkaloid is used to suppress unproductive cough ?
questions.explanation: Codeine is widely used as an antitussive to suppress dry, unproductive coughs.

questions.question_text: Chemical name of Heroin is
questions.explanation: Heroin is chemically known as diacetylmorphine or diamorphine.

questions.question_text: Artemisinin is a
questions.explanation: Artemisinin contains an endoperoxide bridge and is classified as a sesquiterpene lactone.

questions.question_text: An example for indole alkaloid is
questions.explanation: Strychnine is a well-known indole alkaloid found in Strychnos nux-vomica.

questions.question_text: Cholesterol on Oppenauer oxidation gives
questions.explanation: Oppenauer oxidation of cholesterol selectively oxidizes the 3-beta-hydroxyl group to a 3-keto group, yielding cholest-4-en-3-one.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the starting material for the synthesis of Vitamin A ?
questions.explanation: Citral is commonly used as a key starting material in the industrial synthesis of Vitamin A.

questions.question_text: Which of the following xanthine derivative has bronchodilator action ?
questions.explanation: Theophylline is a methylxanthine derivative primarily used for its bronchodilatory effects in asthma and COPD.

questions.question_text: Major blood sugar in insects is
questions.explanation: Trehalose is the primary circulating disaccharide (blood sugar) found in the hemolymph of insects.

questions.question_text: An example for an aromatic amino acid is
questions.explanation: Tryptophan, along with phenylalanine and tyrosine, contains an aromatic ring side chain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used as stabilizer in diethyl ether ?
questions.explanation: Phenyl mercuric nitrate or ethanol is often added to diethyl ether to prevent the formation of explosive peroxides.

questions.question_text: An example for halogenated hydrocarbon type of general anaesthetic drug is
questions.explanation: Halothane is a halogenated alkane used as a general inhalation anesthetic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drug is an amide type of local anaesthetic ?
questions.explanation: Lignocaine (lidocaine) contains an amide linkage, unlike procaine and cocaine which are ester anesthetics.

questions.question_text: Toxic effects of isoniazid can be minimized by administering with
questions.explanation: Isoniazid induces Vitamin B6 deficiency, which can cause peripheral neuropathy; co-administration of pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) prevents this.

questions.question_text: Benzodiazepine overdosage is treated with
questions.explanation: Flumazenil is a specific competitive antagonist at the benzodiazepine binding site on the GABA_A receptor used to reverse overdose.

questions.question_text: In which category of the antipsychotic drugs chlorpromazine belongs to ?
questions.explanation: Chlorpromazine is the prototype aliphatic phenothiazine antipsychotic agent.

questions.question_text: Drug used to treat filariasis is
questions.explanation: Diethylcarbamazine citrate is the drug of choice for the treatment of lymphatic filariasis.

questions.question_text: An alkaloidal drug used as anticholinesterase agent is
questions.explanation: Physostigmine is a naturally occurring alkaloid that acts as a reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor.

questions.question_text: Which vitamin is used to treat beriberi ?
questions.explanation: Beriberi is caused by a deficiency in Vitamin B1, known as thiamine.

questions.question_text: An example for 8-aminoquinoline derivative used as antimalarial drug is
questions.explanation: Primaquine is an 8-aminoquinoline antimalarial drug effective against liver-stage parasites.

questions.question_text: Activation of TLC plates is the process in which ____________ is done.
questions.explanation: Activation of TLC plates involves heating them at an elevated temperature to remove adsorbed moisture.

questions.question_text: ____________ are used in qualitative analysis to find out whether the compounds belong to homologous series.
questions.explanation: R_m values (from chromatography) show a linear relationship with the number of carbon atoms in homologous series.

questions.question_text: The visualizing reagent for cardiac glycosides is
questions.explanation: Kedde's reagent (3,5-dinitrobenzoic acid in alkali) is used to visualize cardiac glycosides on TLC.

questions.question_text: The non-polar stationary phase used in gas-liquid chromatography is
questions.explanation: Polydimethylsiloxane is a standard non-polar stationary phase in gas-liquid chromatography.

questions.question_text: ____________ is a hypothetical functional unit of a column in gas chromatography.
questions.explanation: The theoretical plate is a hypothetical concept used to measure column efficiency in chromatography.

questions.question_text: The fingerprint region of IR spectroscopy is
questions.explanation: The fingerprint region in infrared spectroscopy generally spans from $1500\ \text{cm}^{-1}$ to $400\ \text{cm}^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: ____________ is the father of quality circles, a voluntary group of employees who work on similar tasks.
questions.explanation: Kaoru Ishikawa is widely recognized as the father of quality circles and pioneer of quality management.

questions.question_text: International Conference on Harmonization (ICH) Q 1B guidelines describes

options.B: Photostability testing of new drug substances

questions.explanation: ICH Q1B guideline specifically outlines the requirements for photostability testing of new drug substances and products.

questions.question_text: Hollow Cathode Lamp is a source in ____________ spectroscopy.
questions.explanation: A hollow cathode lamp is the standard radiation source used in atomic absorption spectroscopy.

questions.question_text: Potassium metal when excited in a flame emits ____________ colour.
questions.explanation: When potassium salts are heated in a flame, they emit a characteristic lilac or violet color.

questions.question_text: Indeterminate errors are also called as
questions.explanation: Indeterminate errors are random errors that fluctuate unpredictably from one measurement to another.

questions.question_text: ____________ is an aprotic solvent used in non-aqueous titrations.
questions.explanation: Toluene is an example of an aprotic, non-polar solvent frequently used in non-aqueous titrations.

questions.question_text: The example of fractional precipitation is
questions.explanation: Gay-Lussac's method is a classic example of analytical estimation by fractional precipitation (turbidimetry).

questions.question_text: ____________ is a demasking agent used in complexometric titrations.
questions.explanation: Chloral hydrate is used as a demasking agent to free specific metal ions so they can react with EDTA during complexometric titrations.

questions.question_text: The water content of glacial ethanoic acid for non-aqueous titrations may be in the range
questions.explanation: The acceptable water content in glacial acetic acid (ethanoic acid) for non-aqueous titrations typically ranges from $0.1\%$ to $1\%$.

questions.question_text: ____________ is an indicator electrode used in potentiometric experiments.
questions.explanation: The quinhydrone electrode is a common redox indicator electrode used for pH determinations and potentiometric titrations.

questions.question_text: In polarography, the current which is directly proportional to concentration is
questions.explanation: According to the Ilkovic equation, the diffusion current is directly proportional to the concentration of the electroactive species.

questions.question_text: ____________ is added in modified Volhard's method for determination of chlorides to form an insoluble layer over the precipitate.
questions.explanation: Nitrobenzene is added in the modified Volhard method to coat the silver chloride precipitate and prevent its reaction with thiocyanate.

questions.question_text: The colour change interval of Phenol red indicator is
questions.explanation: Phenol red changes color over a pH range of approximately $6.8$ to $8.4$.

questions.question_text: The theory which states that the colour change of indicators are due to structural changes is
questions.explanation: The quinonoid theory proposes that acid-base indicators undergo structural changes between benzenoid and quinonoid forms, causing color changes.

questions.question_text: The alkaloid containing imidazole ring structure
questions.explanation: Pilocarpine is a plant-derived alkaloid that contains an imidazole ring in its chemical structure.

questions.question_text: The alkaloid which is derived from phenyl alanine is
questions.explanation: Ephedrine is a protoalkaloid derived biosynthetically from the amino acid phenylalanine.

questions.question_text: Anthopleurim is found in the aneural branchial hearts of Pacific Hog Fish used as potent cardiac stimulant.
questions.explanation: Anthopleurim is a peptide isolated from sea anemones known to act as a cardiac stimulant.

questions.question_text: Variablin is the antibiotic principle obtained from Red algae.
questions.explanation: Variablin is a known marine-derived antimicrobial compound found in marine organisms.

questions.question_text: Probiotics are living micro-organisms when taken, improve the intestinal microbial balance.
questions.explanation: Probiotics are defined as live microorganisms that confer a health benefit on the host when administered in adequate amounts.

questions.question_text: Green Hellebore is
questions.explanation: Veratrum viride is commonly known as American white hellebore or green hellebore.

questions.question_text: The crude drug microscopy reveals sunken stomata for
questions.explanation: Ephedra species are xerophytic plants that characteristically possess sunken stomata.

questions.question_text: Spirulina is a blue-green algae possessing immunostimulant activity.
questions.explanation: Spirulina is a cyanobacterium (blue-green alga) known for enhancing immune function.

questions.question_text: The medicinal preparations processed by soaking the drugs in the powdered form in a solution of sugar or jaggery is called
questions.explanation: Asava and Arishta are Ayurvedic preparations made by soaking drugs in sugar/jaggery solutions for fermentation.

questions.question_text: Fine powder of drugs are called as ________ in Ayurveda.
questions.explanation: Choorna is the Ayurvedic term for fine medicinal powder.

questions.question_text: The neurotransmitter released at Autonomic ganglia
questions.explanation: Acetylcholine is the primary neurotransmitter at all autonomic ganglia, acting on nicotinic receptors.

questions.question_text: Penalty imposed for falsely claiming to be a Registered Pharmacist on first conviction as per the Pharmacy Act
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Pharmacy Act, falsely claiming to be a registered pharmacist carries a penalty of imprisonment up to 3 months or fine, or both.

questions.question_text: Analysis and testing of samples of vaccines are carried out at
questions.explanation: The Central Research Institute in Kasauli is a primary national testing laboratory for vaccines and sera in India.

questions.question_text: The bacterium that is most commonly used in genetic engineering
questions.explanation: Escherichia coli (E. coli) is the most widely used host organism in recombinant DNA technology and genetic engineering.

questions.question_text: Monoclonal antibodies are produced by
questions.explanation: Hybridoma technology fuses B-lymphocytes with myeloma cells to continuously produce monoclonal antibodies.

questions.question_text: The immunoglobulin which is seen most abundant in breast milk
questions.explanation: Secretory IgA is the predominant immunoglobulin found in human breast milk, providing mucosal immunity to the newborn.

questions.question_text: Drug license for the retail sale of Schedule C and C1 drugs are issued in
questions.explanation: Form 21 is used for issuing licenses to sell, stock, or exhibit for sale drugs specified in Schedules C and C1.

questions.question_text: Most prokaryotes do not possess
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes generally lack true histones (with some exceptions in Archaea), unlike eukaryotes which wrap DNA around histone proteins.

questions.question_text: Teichoic acid is present in the cell wall of

options.C: Both Gram positive and Gram negative bacteria

questions.explanation: Teichoic acids are unique polymers found specifically within the thick peptidoglycan cell wall of Gram-positive bacteria.

questions.question_text: The nitrogenous base which is absent in RNA
questions.explanation: RNA contains uracil instead of thymine, which is found in DNA.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is not a bactericidal agent?
questions.explanation: Tetracyclines are bacteriostatic antibiotics that inhibit protein synthesis, whereas the others are bactericidal.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not used for the evaluation of disinfectants?
questions.explanation: The Ziehl-Neelsen test is an acid-fast staining technique used for identifying bacteria like Mycobacterium tuberculosis, not for evaluating disinfectants.

questions.question_text: The microscope which gives highest magnification
questions.explanation: Electron microscopes utilize electron beams instead of light, providing significantly higher resolving power and magnification than optical microscopes.

questions.question_text: The process by which very large protein molecules permeates into cells
questions.explanation: Endocytosis is the cellular process by which large molecules and proteins are engulfed and brought into the cell.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has maximum chances of absorption from the gastric mucosa?
questions.explanation: Weak acids like phenobarbital are predominantly unionized in the acidic environment of the stomach, facilitating absorption across the gastric mucosa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Bioavailability of a drug is not true?

options.A: It is a fraction of administered drug that reaches the systemic circulation in an unchanged form
options.B: Bioavailability of an orally administered drug is always less than that of IV administration
options.C: Bioavailability can be determined from plasma concentration or urinary excretion data
options.D: Low oral availability always and necessarily means poor absorption

questions.explanation: Low oral bioavailability can be caused by extensive first-pass metabolism in the liver or gut wall, even if absorption itself is complete.

questions.question_text: Manner of labeling of drugs are specified in the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 as per
questions.explanation: Rule 96 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules specifies the general labeling requirements for drugs.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs does not undergo hepatic first pass effect?
questions.explanation: Insulin is a peptide hormone that is degraded in the gastrointestinal tract and is traditionally administered parenterally, bypassing enteral first-pass metabolism entirely.

questions.question_text: Time for peak plasma concentration ($T_{max}$) indicates
questions.explanation: Peak plasma concentration time ($T_{max}$) is primarily dependent on the rate of drug absorption.

questions.question_text: All of the following except one cross the Blood Brain Barrier
questions.explanation: Dopamine does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier due to its polarity, which is why its precursor levodopa is used clinically instead.

questions.question_text: Any preparation of coca containing more than the following amount of cocaine is considered as a dangerous drug
questions.explanation: Under narcotics regulations, coca derivatives containing more than 0.1% cocaine are classified strictly as dangerous drugs.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a prodrug?
questions.explanation: Clonidine is an active central alpha-2 agonist, whereas Enalapril, Acyclovir (valacyclovir/acyclovir derivatives), and Clopidogrel require metabolic activation.

questions.question_text: The drug which is an inhibitor of Cytochrome P450 enzyme
questions.explanation: Ketoconazole is a potent inhibitor of several CYP450 enzymes (such as CYP3A4), whereas phenytoin, griseofulvin, and phenylbutazone are typically inducers.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs is not metabolized by acetylation?
questions.explanation: Metoclopramide is primarily metabolized by conjugation and oxidation, whereas isoniazid, dapsone, and procainamide undergo N-acetylation.

questions.question_text: The Prevention of Cruelty of Animals Act was enacted in the year
questions.explanation: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act in India was enacted in 1960.

questions.question_text: The drug which is excreted in saliva
questions.explanation: Lithium ions are actively secreted and excreted into saliva, which can sometimes be used for monitoring levels.

questions.question_text: Co-administration of the following drug can result in oral contraceptive failure
questions.explanation: Rifampicin is a strong CYP3A4 inducer that accelerates the metabolism of oral contraceptives, leading to contraceptive failure.

questions.question_text: The clearance and volume of distribution of a drug are $1.5\text{ L/hr}$ and $60\text{ L}$ respectively. What is the predicted half-life of that drug?
questions.explanation: Half-life $t_{1/2} = (0.693 \times V_d) / Cl = (0.693 \times 60) / 1.5 = 27.72\text{ hours}$.

questions.question_text: Percentage of drug remaining in the body after three half lives
questions.explanation: After three half-lives, the remaining fraction of a drug is $(1/2)^3 = 1/8$, which equals 12.5%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a Protease inhibitor?
questions.explanation: Abacavir is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI), whereas ritonavir, atazanavir, and nelfinavir are protease inhibitors.

questions.question_text: As per the Patents Act 1970, the term of every patent from the data of filing of application of patent shall be
questions.explanation: Under the Patents Act 1970, the term of every patent is 20 years from the date of filing of the patent application.

questions.question_text: Long term administration of glucocorticoids can cause all of the following except
questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids cause hypokalemia (potassium loss) and sodium retention, not hyperkalemia.

questions.question_text: The most effective group of drugs for the healing of Non-Steroidal Anti Inflammatory Drug (NSAID) induced gastric ulcer
questions.explanation: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are the most effective agents for both healing and preventing NSAID-induced gastric ulcers.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following anti-asthma drug is not a bronchodilator?
questions.explanation: Nedocromil is a mast cell stabilizer with anti-inflammatory properties, not a direct bronchodilator.

questions.question_text: An incorrect statement regarding histamine is

options.B: Release of catecholamines from adrenal medulla
options.C: Direct action on vascular smooth muscles causing vasodilatation
options.D: Release of EDRF from vascular endothelium resulting in vasodilatation

questions.explanation: Histamine causes vasodilation primarily via endothelial nitric oxide (EDRF) release rather than a direct relaxant action on vascular smooth muscle.

questions.question_text: Hemodialysis is useful in all of the following except
questions.explanation: Digoxin has a very large volume of distribution and high tissue binding, making it ineffective to remove via hemodialysis.

questions.question_text: Apparent Volume of Distribution ($V_d$) is more than total body fluid, if the drug is
questions.explanation: Extensive tissue binding or sequestration results in a low plasma concentration, yielding a high apparent volume of distribution exceeding total body water.

questions.question_text: The anticonvulsant drug that produces weight loss on prolonged use
questions.explanation: Topiramate is well known for causing weight loss as a side effect, unlike valproate and carbamazepine which typically cause weight gain.

questions.question_text: The propellant generally used for topical pharmaceutical aerosols
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons such as propane and butane are commonly used as propellants for topical pharmaceutical aerosols.

questions.question_text: Type I glass used in pharmaceutical packaging is also known as
questions.explanation: Type I glass is highly resistant borosilicate glass used for injectable preparations and sensitive products.
